column1: # Text the CLI draws only while its input prompt is on screen.
# The launcher sends nothing to a session until the pane shows one of these
# and none of the dialogs in startup-blockers.tsv. That makes readiness a
# positive finding. "No known dialog" alone would also describe a pane that is
# still starting, or one showing a dialog that table has no row for, and input
# sent then is typed at whatever comes up next.
# Every row is the status line under the input box: the permission mode the
# session is in, or the shortcuts hint. A startup dialog is drawn before that
# line exists, which is what makes the line evidence that startup is over. The
# prompt glyph itself is deliberately not a row: the same glyph marks the
# focused option in a dialog.
# Columns, tab-separated:
#   id       short name
#   pattern  a literal string that appears in the pane while the prompt shows
# Patterns are matched literally. Blank lines and lines starting with # are
# ignored. Keep a pattern specific enough that it cannot appear in the launch
# command the pane echoes ("--permission-mode acceptEdits" must not match) or
# in a startup dialog.
# Taken from the status-line strings in CLI 2.1.330, where the line reads
# "<mode> on (shift+tab to cycle)". Not yet confirmed against a live pane.
# When a session is at its prompt and the launcher still reports that the
# prompt never appeared, the wording has moved: add a row here.
accept-edits
bypass
plan
auto
dont-ask
manual
shortcuts
